stored_previous_mapping.explanation: preserved_stage_assumption: Exact source counterpart stage groups; Juv. hake: Appendix B: Juvenile Hake. Biomass for juvenile hake (Merluccius productus) was solved for by the model (assuming an EE value of 0.8) since this group was mainly included to be prey for multiple predator species, including adult hake. This group is meant to represent biomass of age 0 and 1 juvenile hake. PB and QB values were taken from other Ecopath models in nearby systems (Ainsworth et al. 2002; Aydin et al. 2007). We found a range of potential values for both, PB = 1.061-2.67 and QB = 5.31-6.98, and taking these ranges to be the 5th and 95th percentiles, we found the mean of the range based on a lognormal distribution. This led to a PB of 1.75 and a QB of 6.1. Diet for juvenile hake came from two different Buckley data sets: Buckley et al. 1999 and unpublished Buckley diet data (T.W. Buckley, unpublished data) for hake for multiple size classes. Using only predator sizes of 20 cm or less, we calculated a diet of 0.2% amphipods, 0.6% epibenthic fauna, 8% copepods, 80% euphuasiids, 1.4% carnivorous zooplankton, 1.4% benthic shrimp, 6% mesopelagic fish, 0.1% cephalopods, 1% juvenile hake (cannibalism), and 0.5% herring. . Existing mapping preserved bit-for-bit. Source zero juvenile catch is a model selectivity proxy, not observed regional stage composition. . See PPR / Allocation assumptions.

stored_previous_mapping.explanation: preserved_stage_assumption: Exact source counterpart stage groups; Juv. rock.: Appendix B: Juvenile Rockfish. This groups consists of juveniles of any and all rockfish species in the California Current, where juveniles are approximately ages 0-2 or the size that can be consumed by a seabird. Production and consumption values were borrowed from Field (2004). Diet was also taken from Field (2004). Biomass was solved for in the model through top-down balancing, using an EE of 0.8.. Existing mapping preserved bit-for-bit. Source zero juvenile catch is a model selectivity proxy, not observed regional stage composition. . See PPR / Allocation assumptions.

stored_previous_mapping.explanation: preserved_stage_assumption: Exact source counterpart stage groups; Juv. rock.: Appendix B: Juvenile Rockfish. This groups consists of juveniles of any and all rockfish species in the California Current, where juveniles are approximately ages 0-2 or the size that can be consumed by a seabird. Production and consumption values were borrowed from Field (2004). Diet was also taken from Field (2004). Biomass was solved for in the model through top-down balancing, using an EE of 0.8.. Existing mapping preserved bit-for-bit. Source zero juvenile catch is a model selectivity proxy, not observed regional stage composition. . See PPR / Allocation assumptions.

stored_previous_mapping.explanation: preserved_stage_assumption: Exact source counterpart stage groups; Juv. round.: Appendix B: Juvenile Roundfish. This group includes juvenile life stage of sablefish (Anoplopoma fimbria) and lingcod (Ophiodon elongatus) species. This group was borrowed from the Field (2004) model. PB, QB, and EE were all borrowed from Field (2004) and biomass was solved for in the model based on top-down balancing. Diet was borrowed from Field (2004) with a few adjustments for the new forage fish groups. Using the diet from Field (2004) and information from the diet study by Brodeur et al. (1987) on consumption of specific forage fish, the diet became: 1.1% amphipods, 81.8% copepods, 12.3% euphasusiids, 2.9% macrozooplankton, 0.1% anchovy, 0.1% herring, 0.1% sandlance, 0.5% whitebait smelt, and 1.1% saury. . Existing mapping preserved bit-for-bit. Source zero juvenile catch is a model selectivity proxy, not observed regional stage composition. . See PPR / Allocation assumptions.

stored_previous_mapping.explanation: preserved_stage_assumption: Exact source counterpart stage groups; Juv. round.: Appendix B: Juvenile Roundfish. This group includes juvenile life stage of sablefish (Anoplopoma fimbria) and lingcod (Ophiodon elongatus) species. This group was borrowed from the Field (2004) model. PB, QB, and EE were all borrowed from Field (2004) and biomass was solved for in the model based on top-down balancing. Diet was borrowed from Field (2004) with a few adjustments for the new forage fish groups. Using the diet from Field (2004) and information from the diet study by Brodeur et al. (1987) on consumption of specific forage fish, the diet became: 1.1% amphipods, 81.8% copepods, 12.3% euphasusiids, 2.9% macrozooplankton, 0.1% anchovy, 0.1% herring, 0.1% sandlance, 0.5% whitebait smelt, and 1.1% saury. . Existing mapping preserved bit-for-bit. Source zero juvenile catch is a model selectivity proxy, not observed regional stage composition. . See PPR / Allocation assumptions.

This includes juvenile life stages of starry flounder (Platichthys stellatus), Pacific sanddab (Citharichthys sordidus), Slender sole (Lyopsetta exilis), Pacific sand sole (Psettichthys melanostictus), Butter sole (Isopsetta isolepis), Rock sole (Lepidopsetta bilineata), English sole (Parophrys vetulus), Petrale sole (Eopsetta jordani), Dover sole (Microstomus pacificus), Rex sole (Glyptocephalus zachirus), and any other Pleuronectiformes species. This group was borrowed from the Field (2004) model. PB, QB, EE, and diet were all borrowed from Field (2004) and biomass was solved for in the model based on top-down balancing. . Existing mapping preserved bit-for-bit. Source zero juvenile catch is a model selectivity proxy, not observed regional stage composition. . See PPR / Allocation assumptions.

rows.reason: Appendix B 'Arrowtooth flounder', paragraph 205 (zero-based) and following group definition. Complete source-model total Yield proportions are a fixed caught-composition proxy across 1950–2019 and all catch bases; source zeros retained as model uncaught assumptions.

rows.reason: Previously adopted identified-regional-catch taxonomic composition is retained. Candidate set: all modeled adult Sebastes groups; juvenile-rockfish catch zero. Constant weights from 1950–2019 identified regional catch assigned directly to candidate groups, filtered to the composite taxon where a pool spans different higher taxa; only direct identified assignments seed weights, so no circular composite weighting. This is a modeled catch-composition projection, not observed composition of unidentified catches. Full candidate set including zero-weight groups: Yellowtail rock., Black rock., Nearshore rock., Yelloweye rock., Greenstriped, Shelf rock., Shortbelly, Canary rock., P. Ocean Perch, Widow rock., Splitnose rock., Slope rock. Source definitions and complete zero/stage candidates have been reassessed; source representative lists are not exhaustive modern-family membership. Preserved regional identified-catch composition (1950–2019) and source-zero juvenile stages. Donor identified catch is whole-LME across1950–2019; target2019 higher-taxon catches can differ by country/fleet, gear, sector, basis and period. No same-reporting-population caught composition is established; pooled taxonomic and reporting-population transfer remains Low confidence.

stored_previous_mapping.explanation: preserved_stage_assumption: Exact source counterpart stage groups; Juv. flat.: Appendix B: Juvenile Flatfish. This includes juvenile life stages of starry flounder (Platichthys stellatus), Pacific sanddab (Citharichthys sordidus), Slender sole (Lyopsetta exilis), Pacific sand sole (Psettichthys melanostictus), Butter sole (Isopsetta isolepis), Rock sole (Lepidopsetta bilineata), English sole (Parophrys vetulus), Petrale sole (Eopsetta jordani), Dover sole (Microstomus pacificus), Rex sole (Glyptocephalus zachirus), and any other Pleuronectiformes species. This group was borrowed from the Field (2004) model. PB, QB, EE, and diet were all borrowed from Field (2004) and biomass was solved for in the model based on top-down balancing. . Existing mapping preserved bit-for-bit. Source zero juvenile catch is a model selectivity proxy, not observed regional stage composition. . See PPR / Allocation assumptions.

stored_previous_mapping.explanation: preserved_stage_assumption: Exact source counterpart stage groups; Juv. rock.: Appendix B: Juvenile Rockfish. This groups consists of juveniles of any and all rockfish species in the California Current, where juveniles are approximately ages 0-2 or the size that can be consumed by a seabird. Production and consumption values were borrowed from Field (2004). Diet was also taken from Field (2004). Biomass was solved for in the model through top-down balancing, using an EE of 0.8.. Production and consumption values were borrowed from Field (2004). Diet was also taken from Field (2004). Biomass was solved for in the model through top-down balancing, using an EE of 0.8.. Existing mapping preserved bit-for-bit. Source zero juvenile catch is a model selectivity proxy, not observed regional stage composition. . See PPR / Allocation assumptions.

rows.reason: Appendix B 'Shelf Rockfish', paragraph 171 (zero-based) and following group definition. Complete source-model total Yield proportions are a fixed caught-composition proxy across 1950–2019 and all catch bases; source zeros retained as model uncaught assumptions.

rows.membership_reason: Source Benthic fish is a documented benthic catch-all. Competing named stocks have different explicit species; source habitat/feeding composition transfer remains weak.

stored_previous_mapping.explanation: preserved_stage_assumption: Exact source counterpart stage groups; Juv. rock.: Appendix B: Juvenile Rockfish. This groups consists of juveniles of any and all rockfish species in the California Current, where juveniles are approximately ages 0-2 or the size that can be consumed by a seabird. Production and consumption values were borrowed from Field (2004). Diet was also taken from Field (2004). Biomass was solved for in the model through top-down balancing, using an EE of 0.8.. Existing mapping preserved bit-for-bit. Source zero juvenile catch is a model selectivity proxy, not observed regional stage composition. . See PPR / Allocation assumptions.

stored_previous_mapping.explanation: preserved_stage_assumption: Exact source counterpart stage groups; Juv. flat.: Appendix B: Juvenile Flatfish. This includes juvenile life stages of starry flounder (Platichthys stellatus), Pacific sanddab (Citharichthys sordidus), Slender sole (Lyopsetta exilis), Pacific sand sole (Psettichthys melanostictus), Butter sole (Isopsetta isolepis), Rock sole (Lepidopsetta bilineata), English sole (Parophrys vetulus), Petrale sole (Eopsetta jordani), Dover sole (Microstomus pacificus), Rex sole (Glyptocephalus zachirus), and any other Pleuronectiformes species. This group was borrowed from the Field (2004) model. PB, QB, EE, and diet were all borrowed from Field (2004) and biomass was solved for in the model based on top-down balancing. . Existing mapping preserved bit-for-bit. Source zero juvenile catch is a model selectivity proxy, not observed regional stage composition. . See PPR / Allocation assumptions.

rows.reason: Appendix B 'Flatfish', paragraph 270 (zero-based) and following group definition. Source Flatfish defines all pleuronectiforms except dedicated halibut/petrale and arrowtooth groups. Dedicated species assigned first. Juvenile-flat catch zero supports adult weight1; this is model selectivity, not an observed regional stage split. Complete source-model total Yield proportions are a fixed caught-composition proxy across 1950–2019 and all catch bases; source zeros retained as model uncaught assumptions.

stored_previous_mapping.explanation: preserved_stage_assumption: Exact source counterpart stage groups; Juv. flat.: Appendix B: Juvenile Flatfish. This includes juvenile life stages of starry flounder (Platichthys stellatus), Pacific sanddab (Citharichthys sordidus), Slender sole (Lyopsetta exilis), Pacific sand sole (Psettichthys melanostictus), Butter sole (Isopsetta isolepis), Rock sole (Lepidopsetta bilineata), English sole (Parophrys vetulus), Petrale sole (Eopsetta jordani), Dover sole (Microstomus pacificus), Rex sole (Glyptocephalus zachirus), and any other Pleuronectiformes species. This group was borrowed from the Field (2004) model. PB, QB, EE, and diet were all borrowed from Field (2004) and biomass was solved for in the model based on top-down balancing. . Existing mapping preserved bit-for-bit. Source zero juvenile catch is a model selectivity proxy, not observed regional stage composition. . See PPR / Allocation assumptions.

rows.reason: Appendix B 'Flatfish', paragraph 270 (zero-based) and following group definition. Source Flatfish defines all pleuronectiforms except dedicated halibut/petrale and arrowtooth groups. Complete source-model total Yield proportions are a fixed caught-composition proxy across 1950–2019 and all catch bases; source zeros retained as model uncaught assumptions.

stored_previous_mapping.explanation: preserved_stage_assumption: Exact source counterpart stage groups; Juv. rock.: Appendix B: Juvenile Rockfish. This groups consists of juveniles of any and all rockfish species in the California Current, where juveniles are approximately ages 0-2 or the size that can be consumed by a seabird. Production and consumption values were borrowed from Field (2004). Diet was also taken from Field (2004). Biomass was solved for in the model through top-down balancing, using an EE of 0.8.. stored_previous_mapping.explanation: preserved_stage_assumption: Exact source counterpart stage groups; Juv. rock.: Appendix B: Juvenile Rockfish. This groups consists of juveniles of any and all rockfish species in the California Current, where juveniles are approximately ages 0-2 or the size that can be consumed by a seabird. Production and consumption values were borrowed from Field (2004). Diet was also taken from Field (2004). Biomass was solved for in the model through top-down balancing, using an EE of 0.8.. Existing mapping preserved bit-for-bit. Source zero juvenile catch is a model selectivity proxy, not observed regional stage composition. . See PPR / Allocation assumptions.

stored_previous_mapping.explanation: preserved_stage_assumption: Exact source counterpart stage groups; Juv. flat.: Appendix B: Juvenile Flatfish. This includes juvenile life stages of starry flounder (Platichthys stellatus), Pacific sanddab (Citharichthys sordidus), Slender sole (Lyopsetta exilis), Pacific sand sole (Psettichthys melanostictus), Butter sole (Isopsetta isolepis), Rock sole (Lepidopsetta bilineata), English sole (Parophrys vetulus), Petrale sole (Eopsetta jordani), Dover sole (Microstomus pacificus), Rex sole (Glyptocephalus zachirus), and any other Pleuronectiformes species. This group was borrowed from the Field (2004) model. PB, QB, EE, and diet were all borrowed from Field (2004) and biomass was solved for in the model based on top-down balancing. . Existing mapping preserved bit-for-bit. Source zero juvenile catch is a model selectivity proxy, not observed regional stage composition. . See PPR / Allocation assumptions.

This includes juvenile life stages of starry flounder (Platichthys stellatus), Pacific sanddab (Citharichthys sordidus), Slender sole (Lyopsetta exilis), Pacific sand sole (Psettichthys melanostictus), Butter sole (Isopsetta isolepis), Rock sole (Lepidopsetta bilineata), English sole (Parophrys vetulus), Petrale sole (Eopsetta jordani), Dover sole (Microstomus pacificus), Rex sole (Glyptocephalus zachirus), and any other Pleuronectiformes species. This group was borrowed from the Field (2004) model. PB, QB, EE, and diet were all borrowed from Field (2004) and biomass was solved for in the model based on top-down balancing. . rows.membership_reason: Primary camera observations establish deep gelatinous/siphonophore feeding. Full competing fish-pool review is retained in analogue_review.json: other jelly-positive forage pools emphasize microplankton/filter feeding, mesopelagics emphasize small deep prey, and Yellowtail/Sablefish emphasize euphausiids/fish; jelly presence alone does not make them eligible. Source35 jelly share23.9234% and52 share36% are supporting evidence, not an optimization criterion. Both still consume much non-gelatinous food and differ in habitat/body size/physiology; source Yield weights are a fixed weak composition proxy.

stored_previous_mapping.explanation: preserved_stage_assumption: Exact source counterpart stage groups; Juv. flat.: Appendix B: Juvenile Flatfish. This includes juvenile life stages of starry flounder (Platichthys stellatus), Pacific sanddab (Citharichthys sordidus), Slender sole (Lyopsetta exilis), Pacific sand sole (Psettichthys melanostictus), Butter sole (Isopsetta isolepis), Rock sole (Lepidopsetta bilineata), English sole (Parophrys vetulus), Petrale sole (Eopsetta jordani), Dover sole (Microstomus pacificus), Rex sole (Glyptocephalus zachirus), and any other Pleuronectiformes species. This group was borrowed from the Field (2004) model. PB, QB, EE, and diet were all borrowed from Field (2004) and biomass was solved for in the model based on top-down balancing. . Existing mapping preserved bit-for-bit. Source zero juvenile catch is a model selectivity proxy, not observed regional stage composition. . See PPR / Allocation assumptions.

stored_previous_mapping.explanation: preserved_stage_assumption: Exact source counterpart stage groups; Juv. flat.: Appendix B: Juvenile Flatfish. This includes juvenile life stages of starry flounder (Platichthys stellatus), Pacific sanddab (Citharichthys sordidus), Slender sole (Lyopsetta exilis), Pacific sand sole (Psettichthys melanostictus), Butter sole (Isopsetta isolepis), Rock sole (Lepidopsetta bilineata), English sole (Parophrys vetulus), Petrale sole (Eopsetta jordani), Dover sole (Microstomus pacificus), Rex sole (Glyptocephalus zachirus), and any other Pleuronectiformes species. This group was borrowed from the Field (2004) model. PB, QB, EE, and diet were all borrowed from Field (2004) and biomass was solved for in the model based on top-down balancing. . Existing mapping preserved bit-for-bit. Source zero juvenile catch is a model selectivity proxy, not observed regional stage composition. . See PPR / Allocation assumptions.

stored_previous_mapping.explanation: preserved_stage_assumption: Exact source counterpart stage groups; Juv. flat.: Appendix B: Juvenile Flatfish. This includes juvenile life stages of starry flounder (Platichthys stellatus), Pacific sanddab (Citharichthys sordidus), Slender sole (Lyopsetta exilis), Pacific sand sole (Psettichthys melanostictus), Butter sole (Isopsetta isolepis), Rock sole (Lepidopsetta bilineata), English sole (Parophrys vetulus), Petrale sole (Eopsetta jordani), Dover sole (Microstomus pacificus), Rex sole (Glyptocephalus zachirus), and any other Pleuronectiformes species. This group was borrowed from the Field (2004) model. PB, QB, EE, and diet were all borrowed from Field (2004) and biomass was solved for in the model based on top-down balancing. . Existing mapping preserved bit-for-bit. Source zero juvenile catch is a model selectivity proxy, not observed regional stage composition. . See PPR / Allocation assumptions.

rows.reason: Unlisted rockfish cannot be declared a member of named single-species stocks. Juvenile all-rockfish and residual Nearshore/Shelf/Slope pools form the closest represented rockfish analogue set; adult habitat composition is unknown. Source Yield weights are fixed proxies, not observed species composition. Complete source-model total Yield proportions are a fixed caught-composition proxy across 1950–2019 and all catch bases; source zeros retained as model uncaught assumptions.

rows.membership_reason: Previously adopted identified-regional-catch taxonomic composition is retained. Candidate set: adult rockfish and thornyhead groups; source juvenile catches zero. Constant weights from 1950–2019 identified regional catch assigned directly to candidate groups, filtered to the composite taxon where a pool spans different higher taxa; only direct identified assignments seed weights, so no circular composite weighting. This is a modeled catch-composition projection, not observed composition of unidentified catches. Full candidate set including zero-weight groups: Yellowtail rock., Black rock., Nearshore rock., Yelloweye rock., Greenstriped, Shelf rock., Shortbelly, Canary rock., P. Ocean Perch, Widow rock., Splitnose rock., Slope rock., Shortspine thorny., Longspine thorny. Source definitions and complete zero/stage candidates have been reassessed; source representative lists are not exhaustive modern-family membership.
rows.allocation_reason: Preserved regional identified-catch composition (1950–2019) and source-zero juvenile stages. Donor identified catch is whole-LME across1950–2019; target2019 higher-taxon catches can differ by country/fleet, gear, sector, basis and period. No same-reporting-population caught composition is established; pooled taxonomic and reporting-population transfer remains Low confidence.

rows.reason: Previously adopted identified-regional-catch taxonomic composition is retained. Candidate set: adult rockfish and thornyhead groups; source juvenile catches zero. Constant weights from 1950–2019 identified regional catch assigned directly to candidate groups, filtered to the composite taxon where a pool spans different higher taxa; only direct identified assignments seed weights, so no circular composite weighting. This is a modeled catch-composition projection, not observed composition of unidentified catches. Full candidate set including zero-weight groups: Yellowtail rock., Black rock., Nearshore rock., Yelloweye rock., Greenstriped, Shelf rock., Shortbelly, Canary rock., P. Ocean Perch, Widow rock., Splitnose rock., Slope rock., Shortspine thorny., Longspine thorny. Source definitions and complete zero/stage candidates have been reassessed; source representative lists are not exhaustive modern-family membership. Preserved regional identified-catch composition (1950–2019) and source-zero juvenile stages. Donor identified catch is whole-LME across1950–2019; target2019 higher-taxon catches can differ by country/fleet, gear, sector, basis and period. No same-reporting-population caught composition is established; pooled taxonomic and reporting-population transfer remains Low confidence.
